description: Baseline websocket realtime benchmark on current streaming pipeline before fixes; overlap/replay dominates the user-visible penalty.

asi.hypothesis: Current choppiness is primarily caused by replayed overlapping streamed audio rather than websocket transport alone.
asi.baseline_observation: Median tune overlap is 13.44s and holdout overlap is 58.24s, far larger than startup latency or chunk deficit.
asi.next_action_hint: Write a regression test around streamed tail accounting in OnnxStreamingAudioDecoder and fix last_emitted_samples bookkeeping before tuning pacing.

description: Tail-bookkeeping fix eliminated overlap on tune prompts, but the benchmark harness timed out on the holdout before completing the run.

asi.hypothesis: Advancing last_emitted_samples after each flush would remove replayed overlapping waveform windows.
asi.observed_partial_result: Tune prompts reached overlap_ms=0 with first_playable_audio_ms around 1.5-1.6s, but max_chunk_deficit_ms jumped to ~1.35-1.39s and chunk counts increased sharply.
asi.rollback_reason: Experiment crashed because BENCH_TIMEOUT_MS=90000 was too low for the longer non-overlapping runs, so the result was not fully measured.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-run from clean baseline with a longer per-turn benchmark timeout, then decide whether the overlap fix is a keep despite exposing severe starvation.
asi.manual_repro: A direct holdout-only websocket run completed in ~44.5s with 31 chunks, suggesting the timeout issue is harness-related rather than a hard product hang.

description: Fix streamed tail bookkeeping so each decode emits only new waveform samples; this removes overlapping replay and makes starvation the next real bottleneck.

asi.hypothesis: The choppy audio was primarily caused by replayed overlapping streamed waveform windows because last_emitted_samples was never advanced after emission.
asi.result_summary: Primary penalty improved 81.5% (15376 -> 2842) and overlap dropped to zero on both tune and holdout prompts.
asi.learned_bottleneck: Once overlap is removed, chunk starvation becomes dominant: max_chunk_deficit_ms is now ~1.3-1.5s and first_playable_audio remains ~1.54s.
asi.next_action_hint: Target pacing and decode granularity next; chunk-count startup gating is likely too coarse now that emitted chunks are true tails.

description: Set the default streaming decode batch to 1 frame to cut first-audio latency, but the benchmark timed out on the third tune prompt.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing stream decode batching from 4 frames to 1 frame would reduce first-playable latency enough to outweigh extra chunk overhead.
asi.observed_partial_result: Tune prompts 1 and 2 improved first_playable_audio_ms to ~0.6s and reduced max_chunk_deficit_ms to ~1.06s, but chunk_count jumped to 51 and 60 and tune:3 exceeded the 180s harness timeout.
asi.rollback_reason: Single-frame flushing increased websocket/message overhead and total response duration enough that the tune suite no longer completed reliably.
asi.next_action_hint: Try an intermediate batch size such as 2 frames, or reduce context retention, to improve slack without exploding chunk count.
asi.partial_prompt_metrics: tune1 first=624ms deficit=1061ms gap=1141ms chunks=51; tune2 first=594ms deficit=1071ms gap=1151ms chunks=60

description: Reduce the default streaming decode batch from 4 frames to 2 frames to improve startup latency and chunk deficit after fixing overlap.

asi.hypothesis: A 2-frame flush size would preserve the overlap fix while reducing the starvation caused by 4-frame 320ms chunks arriving too slowly.
asi.result_summary: Primary penalty improved from 2842 to 2201; first playable audio dropped from 1543ms to 910ms and deficit improved from 1496ms to 1332ms.
asi.tradeoff: Total turn time rose sharply to ~43s and chunk_count increased to 38, so future work should improve throughput without increasing per-turn duration further.
asi.next_action_hint: Test context reduction next, because the first chunk decode cost dropped to 130ms with batch=2 but the steady-state deficit is still >1.2s.

description: Reduce the default streaming decode context from 16 frames to 0 while keeping the 2-frame batch; this removes the main remaining decode-window cost.

asi.hypothesis: Retained decode context was the main remaining throughput bottleneck after moving to true tail emission and a 2-frame batch.
asi.result_summary: Primary penalty improved from 2201 to 1047; first playable dropped to 769ms, chunk deficit fell from 1332ms to 285ms, and total_turn_ms recovered from 43040ms to 13324ms.
asi.learned_bottleneck: Decode-window growth was far more expensive than chunk-count overhead; with context=0 the system is now mostly limited by startup buffering and residual per-chunk delay.
asi.next_action_hint: Attack the output pacer next by switching startup gating from chunk count to buffered-audio duration in milliseconds.

description: Start audio output pacing after 1 chunk instead of 2 so playback begins as soon as the first decoded tail is ready.

asi.hypothesis: With overlap fixed and context removed, the remaining startup delay was mostly self-inflicted by waiting for two chunks before starting playback.
asi.result_summary: Primary penalty improved from 1047 to 784; first playable audio fell from 769ms to 530ms and queue wait effectively disappeared (245ms -> 1ms).
asi.tradeoff: Total turn time and chunk count increased, likely from workload noise and/or longer generated outputs, but holdout penalty improved too and max_chunk_deficit stayed slightly better.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate async/background detokenization next, because the residual 260-284ms deficit likely comes from synchronous decode cost rather than output queueing.

description: Prototype async/background detokenization, but the implementation stalls during final drain and creates ~30s chunk gaps.

asi.hypothesis: Background detokenization could hide decode cost behind frame generation and reduce the remaining ~280ms chunk deficit.
asi.observed_partial_result: First playable audio improved to ~440ms and server_first_decode_ms fell to ~95ms, but a ~30s gap appeared before most chunks were released.
asi.rollback_reason: AsyncStreamingDecoder::finish() waits for the timeout while pending_order is non-empty and does not drain ready completed chunks incrementally, so final audio is held back until the timeout path.
asi.next_action_hint: Add a unit test for AsyncStreamingDecoder::finish() draining ready results without waiting for timeout, then fix the loop and re-run the async experiment.
asi.root_cause_evidence: Tune1 streamed_audio_ms=3680 over 46 chunks, total_turn_ms=34073, and max_binary_gap_ms=29910 — consistent with one early chunk plus a 30s delayed drain.

description: Probe lower text-before-audio interleaving (`LFM2_INTERLEAVED_N_TEXT=1`) to improve first audio, but discard because it massively increases total turn time and chunk count.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing text-before-audio interleaving would let the model begin speaking earlier and maybe lower the realtime penalty.
asi.rollback_reason: Although the primary composite improved to 668ms, total_turn_ms exploded to 123.5s and chunk_count to 430, which is a catastrophic tradeoff and likely prompt-level overfitting rather than a true realtime win.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep default interleaving for now and return to structural decode improvements or a better composite metric if we revisit modality scheduling.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Interleaving ratio strongly affects when audio begins, but the current benchmark is not allowed to trade a 3-5x longer conversation for a few hundred ms of earlier first audio.

description: Retry async/background detokenization with the final-drain bug fixed, but discard because ordered single-frame output still creates multi-second starvation gaps.

asi.hypothesis: Fixing the async final-drain bug would let background detokenization beat the current synchronous path by hiding decode cost behind generation.
asi.rollback_reason: Even with immediate draining, ordered single-frame async output is much worse than the current best: max_chunk_deficit_ms rose to 3545ms and holdout_realtime_penalty_ms to 5344ms.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not revisit single-frame async output; if async returns, keep the current 2-frame batching semantics or use a dedicated detokenizer pool behind the existing chunking model.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Async lowered first_playable_audio_ms to 481ms and server_first_decode_ms to 96ms, but preserving order across many tiny chunks amplified starvation and destroyed smoothness.

description: Probe a moderate text/audio interleaving override (`LFM2_INTERLEAVED_N_TEXT=3`), but discard because it still creates multi-second starvation gaps and hurts holdout behavior.

asi.hypothesis: A smaller but not extreme text-before-audio ratio might improve first audio without the pathological total-turn explosion seen at n_text=1.
asi.rollback_reason: This setting still caused multi-second chunk starvation (max_chunk_deficit_ms 3420, holdout 3991) and materially worsened the primary metric versus the current best 784ms baseline.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop probing interleaving ratios; the workload is too sensitive there. Focus remaining work on decoder-path or client-side smoothing ideas instead.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Interleaving overrides are not a safe realtime lever here: even moderate values can lower first-playable latency while badly harming steady-state smoothness.

description: Increase the default streaming decode batch from 2 frames to 3 frames, but discard because it regresses both startup and holdout smoothness.

asi.hypothesis: A 3-frame batch might preserve most of the 2-frame smoothness while reducing chunk count and per-chunk overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from the best 784ms to 998ms, with first_playable_audio_ms rising to 697ms and holdout_max_chunk_deficit_ms more than doubling to 586ms.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep batch=2. If probing constants further, they should target the pacer or client path, not larger server-side decode batches.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Reducing chunk count from 85 to 37 did not help enough; the extra batching delay outweighed the lower message overhead.

description: Teach the output pacer to catch up immediately when behind schedule, but discard because it slightly regresses the primary metric versus the current best.

asi.hypothesis: When backlog exists, preserving the old schedule instead of resetting from now would let the pacer catch up and reduce residual playout deficit.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 860ms. Although total_turn_ms and chunk_count improved a lot, first_playable_audio_ms and holdout penalty both got slightly worse.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler pacer. Residual deficit is probably dominated by chunk production timing, not pacer catch-up behavior.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Scheduler catch-up is real in isolation, but with the current chunk sizes and decode path it does not produce a better end-to-end websocket result.

description: Probe a longer audio-phase run length (`LFM2_INTERLEAVED_N_AUDIO=24`), but discard because it regresses the primary metric and holdout smoothness.

asi.hypothesis: Longer uninterrupted audio runs might reduce modality-switch overhead and smooth the remaining ~280ms deficit.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 871ms, with first_playable_audio_ms and holdout penalty both worse than the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the default interleaving audio run length. Remaining wins are unlikely to come from modality scheduling constants.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Bigger audio runs reduce neither startup nor deficit enough to beat the current best sync settings.

description: Lower ONNX intra-op threads from 8 to 4, but discard because it clearly regresses startup and chunk deficit on the current best streaming pipeline.

asi.hypothesis: With the current 2-frame/0-context/1-chunk pipeline, fewer ORT intra-op threads might reduce scheduling overhead and improve detokenizer responsiveness.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 1557ms. First playable audio rose to 847ms and max_chunk_deficit_ms jumped to 1309ms.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep ORT intra-op threads at 8. Thread tuning is not the remaining win on this CPU path.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Reducing threads did lower chunk_count, but it delayed chunk production badly enough to hurt both tune and holdout smoothness.

description: Use a 1-frame batch only for the very first audio chunk, then switch back to the 2-frame steady-state batch, but discard because the tune-suite primary regresses.

asi.hypothesis: Combining the fast first chunk of batch=1 with the steadier throughput of batch=2 could improve startup without inheriting the worst single-frame overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 887ms. First playable audio improved to 494ms, but max_chunk_deficit_ms climbed to 393ms and total_turn_ms rose to 25.2s.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler constant 2-frame batching. If startup is revisited, it should be through client-side buffering or a better global scheduling change, not a special-case first chunk.
asi.learned_tradeoff: The first chunk can be made faster, but the extra early decode cadence appears to destabilize later parts of the turn enough to lose overall.

description: Coalesce websocket text deltas to reduce text chatter during streaming, but discard because audio smoothness still regresses versus the current best.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing per-token text websocket traffic might free enough scheduling headroom to improve audio chunk delivery without changing final text semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 934ms. First playable audio and chunk deficit both got worse despite lower chatter.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat text-delta coalescing as a UX cleanup idea, not a realtime optimization. Remaining wins are unlikely to come from websocket text traffic.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Audio starvation appears dominated by generation/decode cadence, not by the cost of sending every text update over the websocket.

description: Increase the stream-event channel capacity from 64 to 256 to reduce producer backpressure, but discard because it does not beat the current best websocket result.

asi.hypothesis: If the model worker is occasionally blocked by the bounded stream-event channel, a larger buffer could reduce backpressure and improve audio chunk timing.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 835ms, with slightly worse first_playable_audio_ms and holdout penalty. Queue wait was already ~1ms, so channel capacity was not the main bottleneck.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop probing stream-channel capacity. Remaining work should assume chunk production cadence, not channel backpressure, is the limiting factor.
asi.learned_tradeoff: A much larger producer buffer does not materially change max_chunk_deficit_ms on this workload, which strongly suggests websocket send backpressure is not dominating.

description: Disable server-side startup pacing entirely and let playback start on the first available chunk, but discard because it still loses to the current best configuration.

asi.hypothesis: Removing startup pacing entirely might let the browser queue absorb jitter better than the current 1-chunk server-side pacer.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed from 784ms to 855ms and holdout penalty also worsened. The simpler 1-chunk pacer still gives a better overall tradeoff.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the 1-chunk startup pacer. Remaining wins are unlikely to come from more server-side pacing tweaks.
asi.learned_tradeoff: Immediate-start pacing reduced total_turn_ms and chunk_count but did not improve the actual audio smoothness metric enough to beat the current best.
